title: Faithfulness of L_S (edge-induced, not principal submatrix) + uniformity of c over all G, ε and degenerate cases

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Faithfulness (F1) + uniformity/edge cases (F2): two gaps not covered by q6-17/18/20.**

**(A) Definitional faithfulness — $L_S$ is NOT the principal submatrix.**
The object is
$$L_S=\sum_{(u,v)\in E:\,u,v\in S} (\delta_u-\delta_v)(\delta_u-\delta_v)^\top \in \mathbb{R}^{V\times V},$$
the Laplacian of the *edge-induced* subgraph $G_S=(V,E(S,S))$ on the **full** vertex set $V$. Two silent substitutions would make a proof answer the wrong question:
- replacing $L_S$ by the **principal submatrix** $L[S,S]$ (this includes the boundary-degree diagonal from edges $E(S,\bar S)$, so $L[S,S]\ne L_S$ in general — e.g. a star with $S=$ leaves has $L_S=0$ but $L[S,S]=I$);
- replacing $L_S$ by $\varepsilon^2 L$ or by a degree-thresholded surrogate (drift toward a "low-degree set" heuristic).
The proof must use $L_S$ exactly as defined at every step. Key structural facts that any argument should explicitly use and that distinguish $L_S$:
  (i) boundary edges $E(S,\bar S)$ contribute **nothing** to $L_S$ (free slack — this is why an independent set is light for all $\varepsilon$ since then $L_S=0\preceq\varepsilon L$);
  (ii) $\mathrm{range}(L_S)\subseteq\mathrm{range}(L)$, and $\ker L\subseteq\ker(\varepsilon L-L_S)$, so PSD-ness need only be checked on $\mathrm{range}(L)$;
  (iii) downward closure $S'\subseteq S\Rightarrow L_{S'}\preceq L_S$ (used by the q6-18 alteration argument — but it must be proved: $L_S-L_{S'}=\sum_{(u,v)\in E(S,S)\setminus E(S',S')}b_{uv}b_{uv}^\top\succeq0$).

**(B) Uniformity of $c$ over ALL $G$ and ALL $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, including degenerate inputs.**
The constant $c$ must be independent of $n=|V|$, of density, of the spectral gap, and of $\varepsilon$. A complete proof must dispatch:
- $\varepsilon\to0^+$: the bound only requires $|S|\ge c\varepsilon n$, which may be $<1$; check the claim is vacuous/satisfied when $c\varepsilon n<1$ (a single vertex $S=\{v\}$ has $L_S=0\preceq\varepsilon L$, always light), and that for $c\varepsilon n\ge1$ the construction delivers an integer-size set.
- $\varepsilon\to1^-$: must still produce $|S|\ge cn$.
- **Disconnected $G$ / isolated vertices / $L$ singular**: $L$ has nontrivial kernel (one dimension per component); verify PSD-ness is correctly interpreted on $\mathrm{range}(L)$ and that isolated vertices (which can be added to $S$ for free, contributing $0$ to $L_S$) are exploited or at least not mishandled.
- **$E=\varnothing$**: $L=0$, every $S$ is light; trivial but should be acknowledged.
- The final $c$ must be stated as an explicit number (or explicit expression), consistent across the sparse/dense case split if one is used.

**Acceptance criterion.** The proof names $L_S$ by its edge-induced definition wherever used, proves (i)–(iii), and exhibits a single universal constant $c>0$ with the size bound holding for every $G$ and every $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$ including all degenerate cases above.
